tex_content.html:
The quantity $Q=R(q,0)$ is bounded above by a universal constant. \end{claim}
Proof

\sketch ↗ claim:distance-bound-under-rescaling The integrated Harnack inequality and the distance claim give $R(q,-cQ^{-1})\leq \exp (\widetilde C(c)^2/(2c))$ because $R(p,0)=1$. After rescaling by $Q$, Shi estimates on $B(q,2)$ imply $\partial _tR(q,t)\leq C''Q^2$ for $-Q^{-1}<t\leq 0$. Therefore

\[ Q\leq cC''Q+\exp (\widetilde C(c)^2/(2c)). \]

Taking $c=(2C'')^{-1}$ gives a universal upper bound.

□

\begin{claim} \end{claim}[Universal neighborhood curvature bound]
